case.title: Epileptic spasms and developmental regression
case.brief:
Referral from paediatric neurology. A girl developed normally until 7 months, when epileptic spasms began with hypsarrhythmia on her EEG. She has lost skills and has axial hypotonia; her MRI is normal. Now 14 months, she still has spasms despite vigabatrin and prednisolone.

Trio exome sequencing, analysed with the epilepsy panel, found a heterozygous SCN2A variant, NM_001040142.2:c.2558G>A p.(Arg853Gln), absent from both parents. The exome confirms both parents are her biological parents.
tasks: Score the de novo evidence with ClinGen’s points: this patient, and others you find in ClinVar and the literature. PS2 or PM6, and how strong?
Compare the missense predictors with their calibrated thresholds. What strength of PP3 do the ACGS and ClinGen allow?
Look at the protein: where is the variant, and are pathogenic missense variants clustered there?
Classify, sign and compare with the ClinGen Epilepsy Sodium Channel expert panel.
case.source: Variant: NM_001040142.2(SCN2A):c.2558G>A, GRCh38 2-165342465-G-A, ClinGen allele CA210022 (absent from gnomAD v4.1). ClinVar VCV000194555; ClinGen Epilepsy Sodium Channel VCEP classification (Evidence Repository). Checked October 2026. The patient and family are fictional.

patients.ref: Case 5: infant with epileptic spasms and developmental regression
patients.referral: Paediatric neurology: epileptic spasms from 7 months with hypsarrhythmia, and loss of skills.
patients.summary: Girl of 14 months. Normal development until 7 months, when epileptic spasms began; the EEG showed hypsarrhythmia. She has since lost her smile and her interest in toys, and has axial hypotonia. MRI brain normal. Spasms continue despite vigabatrin and prednisolone.
patients.familyHistory: Parents unrelated and well; older brother well. No family history of epilepsy.
patients.notes: Fictional patient and family; the variant and the published evidence about it are real.

expected.source: ClinGen Epilepsy Sodium Channel expert panel (VCEP), Evidence Repository, specifications v1.0.0; ClinVar VCV000194555 (Pathogenic, reviewed by expert panel, 2023-05-09).

notes.PS2: De novo with maternity and paternity confirmed in at least four published people with consistent phenotypes; this patient is another (the trio exome confirms parentage). Under the panel’s current specification (v2.0) each such person with a complex neurodevelopmental disorder scores 1 point: 2 points is strong, 4 very strong.
notes.PS3: Patch-clamp studies: peak sodium current 51% of normal.
notes.PM1: In a region of the channel enriched for pathogenic variants.
notes.PM2: Supporting: absent from gnomAD (v4.1, and v2.1.1 when the panel curated it).
notes.PP3: Moderate: REVEL 0.95, above the panel’s threshold of 0.773 (Pejaver et al. 2022). The ACGS 2024 guidelines would use PP3 at supporting strength only.
